chapter: Guitar, John Collins and Ellington on the radio
title: Why Chicago musicians went into real estate; Jones leaves for New York
summary: Chicago could not support a musician with a family, so players moved to other work; Jones went to New York without knowing what would happen.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Because that seemed to be the thing around Chicago in those days, because it didn't have the thing that New York had at that time. You had to leave Chicago if you were going to be in this business that I'm in. So the guys would end up buying property and going into real estate and playing music on the side, you know? That was the -- those were the social overtones there, then, at that time.
It wasn't possible to earn a good living in music in Chicago.

No. You could -- if you were young, you could get around a little bit, you know, but as time went, especially if a man had a family, and responsibilities, the best thing for him to do was just to get into something which is seemingly more stable, you know? But I was just possibly very fortunate when I went to New York, and had no idea what was
going to happen. I didn't -- I kept my keys at home with my mother's sister, my aunt, in case I had to come back, you know. You don't know how you're going to turn out, you know.
